question: What downward camera tilt do 2.webp and 10.webp need, and how was it chosen?
why: measure.js and compare.js both pinned c.pitch = 0, so the harness could not reproduce any photograph shot looking down. 10.webp puts the pool's far edge at 0.41 of frame height -- above the horizon -- which a level camera cannot produce at any yaw or fov.
criterion: Alignment of the MEASURED water-band rows between render and photograph (longest contiguous cyan run per column). Explicitly NOT dE2000: dE was recorded at every step and used to choose nothing.
signCorrection: controls.pitch feeds camera.rotation.x, where POSITIVE looks UP. Established by sweep, not assumed -- the first draft had it backwards and moved the horizon away from the photograph. main.js negates, so a positive config value reads as 'tilted N degrees down'.

candidates.note: at pitch 0 the longest cyan run is the SKY, 0.0-0.373; the water is 0.62-1.0

10.webp.analyticCrossCheck: Solving 0.5 - 0.5*(Y/Z)/tan(36) = 0.41 for the far coping edge at 11.20 m along-axis and 1.91 m below the eye gives 17.1 degrees. The swept answer is 22. The gap is expected and is NOT noise: the analytic route assumes the photograph shares the render's 72-degree legacy vertical fov, and serenity's meta.photoFovLong (120) has never been audited -- kings-court's identical 120 measured at ~57-58 by two independent methods and is routed to plan 5. The swept value matches an observable; the analytic one matches a model with an unverified parameter, so the sweep wins.

honesty: This is an INSTRUMENT correction, not a rendering improvement. Nothing about how the scene is lit, shaded or drawn changed in task 1b; the harness simply stopped capturing a camera the photographer never used. Report it as such wherever the number appears, the same way plan 4b reported its own movement.
routed: The other nine serenity spots and all thirteen kings-court spots are still captured at pitch 0, and every one of them was pose-verified under that constraint. If any of those photographs was shot with tilt, the same correction is available and unclaimed. Not swept here -- that is a second pass over every camera in both flats, which is plan 4b's work redone, and it needs its own before/after. Routed to 4d.
